glossary.definition: The Elixir/Phoenix daemon that owns canonical truth (control plane, lineage, routing). System of record.
The OTP application that boots the control plane, sessions, babysitter, and surfaces supervisors. "If you run one thing, run this."
The execution substrate / API server. Runs sessions, tools, memory, skills, delegation. Strongest current candidate for the meta-harness router.
A user-facing shell (Discord / web / CLI / native desktop / editor). Mirrors and controls; **does not own state.**
Repo-/space-owned durable artifacts (plans, handoffs, notes, exports, context bundles). Human-readable AND agent-readable.
A live multi-user / multi-agent editable artifact: doc, wiki page, canvas, thread. Distinct from workspace artifacts and from control-plane records.
An append-only authoritative event in EMA: proposal, execution, dispatch_update, incident, host_transition, etc.
The chain of control-plane records linking an intent to its runtime outcome. Must remain explicit and replayable.
Live runtime continuity for an actor (human or agent) talking to a runtime. Has a session_id distinct from execution_id and from provider_session_id.
A typed adapter that takes an EMA dispatch and runs it on a specific harness/runtime. Sits **above** raw model providers.
`hermes-native`, `claude-cli`, `codex-cli`, `peer-remote`, `simulated-tui`.
A model API endpoint (Anthropic, OpenAI, local). Strictly below drivers. **Not interchangeable with "driver" or "runtime".**
The execution shell around a model invocation (CLI, in-process runtime, peer worker). A driver picks one.
Watchdog/scheduler tier that supervises long-running execution chains and takes over stalled work. OpenClaw doctrine, crystallized in Elixir.
The principle that tools/auth/resources differ across human shells, agent turns, daemons, surfaces, and machines. Orchestration must respect this.
Explicit choice of where a dispatch runs: `local` / `daemon` / `peer` / host-affinity. Not a hidden implementation detail.
Top-level administrative + security boundary. Owns members, projects, billing, policy bundles, peer-trust roots.
The unit each EMA instance binds to. Owns an event_log shard, a workspace root, sessions, harness policy, datasets. Belongs to one Org or one User (personal).
Collaboration scope inside an Org, orthogonal to Projects. Owns membership-with-roles, channels/threads, collaboration objects.
Versioned, addressable input bundle bound to a Project (or Org-shared). Distinct from workspace artifacts.
Human or agent identity participating in an Org/Space, with role and permissions. Agent identities may be first-class — see Open Question Q1.
A user-level agent identity with implicit access to all Projects/Spaces the user belongs to, gated by per-Org policy.
A virtual app inside the EMA shell (Wiki, Chat, Threads, Agent vEnv, Blueprint, Code, etc.). Rendered inside Launchpad / Virtual Desktop.
Top-level launcher surface (Win8/Start-style) hosting vApps.
Per-user, per-project dashboard surface. Personal HQ aggregates across all Projects/Orgs.
The main interface metaphor inherited from place.org — accessible as a native desktop app or as a website.
EMA-native replacement for Discord channels/threads, mirrored back to Discord via webhook during transition.
Knowledge-structuring artifact (Karpathy-style) that integrates with the Wiki and intent capture.
Earlier multi-agent / Discord-native operator system. Doctrine donor (roles, handoffs, watchdogs), not the final architecture.
Earlier TypeScript Discord/web operator surface. Donor of the surface↔Hermes interface contract.
Earliest browser-native virtual-desktop / "place" lineage. Donor of UX metaphor (Launchpad, HQ, Desktop).
Strategic future direction — peer-aware execution and collaboration on a BEAM-family base. Deferred until local semantics pin down.
Lessons/patterns extracted from a prior era; carried forward as design principles, not as code.
Personal / Organization / Shared / Ghost / Public — fundamental isolation unit owning files, tasks, agents, vault, channels, keys, and sync policy. Disambiguates the bare "Space" entry above.
Ephemeral collaboration space with TTL, ephemeral keys, and self-destruct semantics for temporary multi-party work. Distinct from durable Workspace and Collaboration object.
Per-Space inbox for raw thoughts that gets auto-classified into tasks, notes, proposals, or journal entries. The capture-before-classify intake surface.
Pre-queue check (vault precedent + preferences + corrections + confidence ≥ 0.85) that lets agents resolve silently instead of escalating to human review.

Required metadata header on every agent-to-agent handoff carrying status, confidence, completeness, and provenance alongside the payload. Distinct from execution lineage — a per-edge reliability contract.
XML `<background-results>` wrapper that injects async agent outcomes back into a live session in a uniform format. Inter-agent async result-injection format above raw provider streaming.

Express/WebSocket server that mediates between a surface (Agent OS WebUI) and back-end engines (OpenClaw, Discord, Vault, Dispatch). Concrete prior art for the surface↔runtime mediator distinct from Driver and Harness.
Surface-design stance treating the operator UI as an ambient awareness layer (calm-technology) rather than a chat app with bots. UX doctrine behind Launchpad/HQ/Threads.
Always-on pre-routing reasoning tier that does intent parsing, metaprompting, and prompt consulting on every inbound request before any dispatch. Upstream of Driver/Harness.
Three-subsystem layer (metabolism = activation decay, graph = typed edges, cognition = injection/contradiction/gap detection) that turns the vault into an active participant.
Embedding/index/query infrastructure that gives every EMA item a semantic fingerprint and powers the `context_for/2` injection function.
External user-modeling/peer-representation service (Plastic Labs) used for pre-dispatch scope advice and post-execution reflexion injection.
Pre-dispatch component that queries Honcho/user-model context to advise on scope and approach before an agent is spawned. Distinct from router/driver selection.

HTTP/stdio server inside the EMA daemon that exposes EMA's tools (vault search, task CRUD, proposals, project context, executions) to Claude agents via MCP. Outbound tool-exposure boundary (complement to inbound Driver/Provider).
Mesh capability where a rate-limited EMA node routes Claude/inference calls through a peer node's credentials, sharing capacity without exposing keys. Sharpens Placement semantics.
